## Current focus

Phases 4 and 5 (integrations and the requested polish) have landed. Jade shows each carcass's next step, the tool it
needs, and bleeding and acid progress, plus the skin rack's state. An "Alex's Mobs" category ships in Butchery's
Patchouli guide. Seven advancements sit under Butchery's tree, and Butchery's own chain is granted where our blocks
stand in for its. Farmer's Delight cutting recipes are included, along with acid-made skeleton blocks and four pelt
rugs. The renderer now draws multipart bodies, catfish sizes and each renderer's own size, and centres heads on
their geometry. A per-mob gallery in the smoke test (`run/screenshots/smoketest_mob_<mob>.png`, side-on) was
reviewed for all 82 mobs.

## Decisions

- Blocks and items are registered by looping `def/MobDefs` and `def/ItemDefs`; the auto inventory above therefore
  lists almost nothing. Add a mob by adding a table row, then `runData`.
- Carcass `blockstate` numbering is Butchery's (fresh 0/1; drained hanging 1-5, ground 0, 6-9; skinless fresh 4-6 / 7-9)
  so Butchery's tag-driven hints, drips, apron and advancements work unchanged. Do not renumber.
- Fresh/drained carcasses render Alex's Mobs' models through `client/render/CarcassScene`. `StageTextures` composites
  terrapin appearance layers before draining. `StageGeometry` fits separate muscle and skeletal meshes to the model's
  local boxes, retaining its hierarchy and posing; tissue materials do not inherit coat markings. Fully transparent
  source cubes stay absent (alternate tusks/antlers). Borrowed mesh lists and visibility are restored after rendering.
- `HangingPose` brings profile hind legs inward at their joints and seats an actual mesh surface directly on the
  hook bowl/rope knot, using the support's own facing. There is no generated sling. The remaining surface area
  balances beneath the attachment; cuts and skeletons are fitted to their own visible geometry.
  `hanging.legs`/`forelegs`, `leg_pitch`, and `pitch` distinguish vertical quadrupeds, inverted bipeds and tail-up bodies.
  Ordered `hanging.attachment` parts select solid anatomy instead of fins or tentacles (`binding` remains a legacy
  alias). Forelegs and tails fall from their joints; `hanging.rotations` specifies absolute local XYZ angles in
  degrees for authored poses such as the octopus's folded arms. Joint lengths and living models are preserved.
  Sampled attachment layouts have a bounded cache, cleared with model/texture caches; borrowed rotations are restored.
- Cuts reduce the remaining tissue and expose ribs, including tailless mobs. Multipart cuts shorten the chain while
  keeping surviving segments whole. Already skeletal mobs retain their original geometry/material (`skeletal` profile
  flag). Turtle shells disappear at CUT_1, when their shell item drops.
- The client smoke test checks actual emitted vertices for all 82 mobs, all 61 skeletons, variant pixels, and model
  restoration after normal and interrupted renders. `smoketest_asset_*.png` compares stages and terrapin variants.
- Drops go through `LivingDropsEvent`; Butchery's `/kill` cleanup is not reproduced. Items in
  `#alexsbutchery:replaced_by_carcass` are removed from a carcass kill, everything else the mob drops is kept.
- The tags `butchery_alexs_mobs:*` belong to the official add-on and are never shipped here; blood is drained by
  calling Butchery's fill procedures directly (`compat/ButcheryHooks`).
- Butchery's skin rack cannot show new skins, so hanging ours swaps the block for `alexsbutchery:skin_rack`, which
  reuses Butchery's salted/wet/leather rack models and swaps Butchery's empty rack back.
- Items another installed mod already has are substituted at drop time (`compat/Substitutions`) and hidden from tabs.
- Pose profiles are keyed by mob id (`pose_profiles/<mob>.json`), not entity id; the centipede's entity is
  `centipede_head`. The smoke test fails if any mob lacks its own profile.
- `CarcassModels` calls each renderer's `LivingEntityRenderer#scale` hook (SRG `m_7546_`) on a scratch pose per
  snapshot: Alex's Mobs picks its model there (catfish sizes, anaconda/bone serpent/void worm segment types, bison,
  blobfish) and sets its size. Only the uniform scale is kept; riding translations are dropped.
- Multipart bodies are drawn from the segment entities' own renderers, placed by the profile's `segments` block
  (spacing from Alex's Mobs' spawn code): coiled or S-curved lying, hanging straight by the tail.
- Heads (block, trophy, rug) are centred on the head part's box, turned by its rotation, and rest on their surface.
- Patchouli 1.20 dropped book `extend`; the pages ship in Butchery's namespace
  (`assets/butchery/patchouli_books/butchers_guide/en_us/{categories,entries}/alexsbutchery*`), generated by
  `data/ModGuideBook` from the mob table. They are literal English, as Butchery's book is not i18n.
- Our advancements hang under `butchery:butcher`; criterion `alexsbutchery:butchering` (action, mob, floor) is
  open to packs. Butchery's own chain (`firstcarcass`, `hangingaround`, the skin rack steps) is granted from our
  handlers only once its parent is done, as Butchery does.
- Farmer's Delight cutting turns our raw meats into its generic cuts (minced beef, chicken cuts, bacon, cod
  slices), conditional on `farmersdelight`, like Butchery's own beef/pork/mutton conversions.
- Acid (`butcher/Acid`) dissolves a whole carcass (state 0 or 1, fresh or drained, not bleeding) in 220 ticks
  counted in the block entity; `SkeletonBlock` is an `AbstractCarcassBlock`, so skeletons hang on hooks too.
  Bleeding mobs and fish have skeletons; bloodless mobs, both mosquitoes, the giant squid, the Void Worm and the
  Murmur do not (`MobDef.hasSkeleton`).
- A rug is a block model (`models/block/rug.json`, pelt texture from `art/butchery_art.py`) plus the mob's head drawn
  by the block entity renderer; three pelts around the head craft it.

## Known issues

- Butchery's own log noise in dev: its ravager model has an invalid rotation and its Farmer's Delight recipes/tags
  reference missing items when Farmer's Delight is absent. Not ours.
- `check_mod.py` notes one "item model without item" per loop-registered item; false positives. Its one warning
  (`skin_rack` has no item) is by design.
- Forge's `PlayerAdvancements.award` refuses FakePlayers; GameTests that check advancements use a plain
  `ServerPlayer` borrowing a FakePlayer's no-op connection (`TestSupport.advancementPlayer`).
- The smoke-test window is tiled by Hyprland, so screenshots come out 1900x566 rather than 1280x720.
